title: Explainable AI is Responsible AI: How Explainability Creates Trustworthy and Socially Responsible Artificial Intelligence

bias_targets.methodology: The paper reviews literature utilizing XAI techniques (such as LIME, SHAP, and counterfactuals) and disparity scores (like Wasserstein distance) to reveal and mitigate gender bias in applications such as juvenile recidivism prediction, medical diagnostics, and ADHD diagnosis.

The paper surveys studies that apply disparate impact assessments and XAI tools to identify racial and ethnic discrimination in predictive policing, facial recognition, and medical diagnostic systems.
The paper highlights literature using LIME scoring and fairness metrics to evaluate bias against foreigners (nationality as a static input) in juvenile recidivism prediction models.

The paper discusses the use of custom XAI auditing frameworks to evaluate disparity scores based on socioeconomic factors, such as insurance status in medical diagnostics and disparate impact in loan decision-making models.
The paper reviews literature examining inherited human biases regarding age in the decision-making algorithms of autonomous vehicles (e.g., through the Moral Machine Experiment).
